questions: Do you have weakness in either arm or leg?
Do you have numbness or altered sensation on one side of your body?
Have you had episodes of shaking or jerking that you cannot control?
Do these episodes occur only when you are awake?
Have you ever lost consciousness during one of these episodes?
Do your symptoms improve when your attention is distracted?
Do your shaking episodes tend to start or worsen during emotional stress or interpersonal conflict?
Did the episodes begin after a frightening, traumatic, or highly stressful life event?
Do you feel distressed or anxious immediately before an episode?
Do the jerks continue unchanged during objectively confirmed sleep?
Can you voluntarily suppress a jerk for a short time?
Do you experience a premonitory urge or rising inner tension before a jerk that is relieved afterward?
Did the jerks begin after starting or increasing a medication, including an antidepressant, antipsychotic, stimulant, anti-nausea drug, or antiseizure drug?
Do the jerks occur in multiple body regions rather than remaining confined to one limb?

served: video-EEG monitoring with limb surface electrodes
distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side)
entrainment testing (tap to an externally paced rhythm)
variability of amplitude, frequency and axis over the examination
